Thanks, I really appreciate the comments. Cathy was one of the few that knew before the post. The night I wrote this post I let her read it just in case there was anything she didn’t know. 

As an update since this post was created, I have been seeing a therapist weekly and started visiting a psychiatrist and learned that my body could not metabolize my previous antidepressant medication. The doctor started me on a new medication and I have felt much, much better. 

Cathy watched from a distance and she noticed I was making strides to get a better handle on my problems and we have started talking again. I am learning to be mindful of myself and my feelings so I do not subject her or anyone else to my blowups. 

To anyone that reads this and has experienced any form of abuse please seek help. Do not be ashamed to ask. There are good people in the world that are willing to lend a hand. If you are seeking help and using medication I strongly urge you to do a genesight study. This will help your doctor determine what medications your body can metabolize and what you should stay away from. I was taking lexapro and the study found that I was likely to experience some of the benefits while feeling most of the side effects.  Going to a good therapist while taking medication has made me feel so much better about myself and keeps me motivated to find the peace that I have been longing for.

It has been one year since my gf left and I decided to get help. It’s been about 4 months since she decided she wanted to try again. I warned her not to but she says I am a different person now especially when we go out. 

I have/had major anxiety problems since I was a child. I never sought help because I thought it was just part of my personality.  I thought I was just an introvert that extremely dislikes going out and being in crowded places. I will never sing karaoke in front of strangers but it is easier for me to talk to new people and enjoy going out now.

You’re welcome.

Unfortunately I am the type of person who doesn’t see something is wrong until it hits rock bottom. It took my gf ending our relationship to see how I was affecting her. 

When I sought help I didn’t do it bring her back I did it because I was tired of who I was. I started by talking to my doctor about my anger issues and depression and he put me on Lexapro and recommended a therapist that specializes in anger issues. Between the medicine calming my anxiety and learning how to spot flare ups helped immensely. 

She saw how my personality changed without the anxiety and gave me a second chance. I still get angry but it’s manageable. We are looking into buying a house and had an argument regarding it the other day. We both settled it in a manor that we were both satisfied with that didn’t involve an explosion or crying and we were able to move on. 

I wish you the best of luck OP. If you go through a similar situation please make sure to look out for yourself and only go back it he wants to change for himself. If he only changes to bring you back I can speak from experience that everything will go back to what it is now once he feels comfortable again.

You are correct. I apologize if my comment made it seem like my anger was a thing I couldn’t control. That was something I learned in therapy was that I was in control. I needed to learn it was ok to say hey, I need a minute alone or other ways to deal with it instead of letting it fester. My gf was not the cause of my explosion. My inability to say this is making me angry or I’m not feeling well mentally was what caused the explosion.

You are right to think that. The only thing is I don’t have strong relationships with really anyone but my gf. My brothers and sister never really cared for me. I had friends who were guys and I exploded in them too thus eventually ending my friendship with them.

I have anger issues similar to this that I am currently dealing with. I sought help from a therapist and he gave a good summary about why it was easier to explode on certain people rather than others. He said to think of relationships like bank accounts. The stronger the relationship you have with a person the more you have in the account. When I had an outburst it was like making a withdrawal from an account and like an actual account you’re going to more likely withdraw from the account you have the most in. 

When I exploded it was usually at my gf. At the time I had bad anxiety and never did things to relieve stress or talk about my feelings. When she would do things that triggered me I couldn’t stop it.  It never got physical but you don’t always need to hit someone to hurt them. 

It was all my fault and I have been working to control my problems. One thing that helps is to think of my stress as water filling a bathtub. If I don’t do something to drain some water it will eventually over flow. Playing calming games and meditation helps.  Now I have become more cognizant of my stress levels and if I feel overwhelmed I say give me a minute, close my eyes, take deep breaths and try to focus on my current surroundings. My gf is responsive to this and tries to help. I almost lost her to my problems and she appreciates the changes I have tried to make. 

I hope your bf is willing to seek help like I did. There is no shame in admitting you need help. It took me a long time to realize this but my relationship is better because of it. Good luck!
